reviews.review: Fun times beating up orks. Last level of the game and final fight are bad, but everything up until then is a lot of fun and makes up for the weak ending. The multiplayer is alright but could be better.
Great singleplayer, but don't expect anything from the multiplayer

"An open mind is a fortress with its gates unbarred and unguarded."

What can be said about Space Marine? Did it change the world or set it on fire? No. Did it revolutionize... anything? No. It's a bog-standard Third Person Shooter/Brawler. That being said, as you play this game you feel like one of the Emperor's Angels of Death, stomping, slashing, and bolting through His enemies and bringing holy retribution down on the Heretic, the Mutant, and the Xenos.

This product has been deemed free of heresy by the Ordo Malleus and is required learning for all. May the Astronomican burn brightly for all eternity. May His light guide us in our Holy Rage.

Warhammer 40,000: Space Marine is a game that involves the Ultramarines, Orcs and Daemons. The overall of the storyline without spoilers is for Space Marine to take back the planet that the Orcs have conquered. This review is conducted in a manner where I have not played any Warhammer 40,000 games, and Space Marine is my first one, so I would not know if there is a continuing storyline. This review does not contain Multiplayer comments, only single player.

Campaign: Space Marine includes a solid campaign. The campaign clocks in for me at 8.5 hours on "normal" difficulty. As stated without spoilers, the elements of the orcs, the ultra marines and eventually the daemons add a lot of twists to the storyline that make the game interesting. Throughout the campaign, you get that feeling that "oh wow, the game is about to finish and this is a great way to finish it", but it extends to another chapter, which is good, however whilst that happens a few times, it does drag. The ending was strong and gave me excitement for a new Warhammer, which most likely will not happen. The campaign involves sections that overwhelm the player (and you know, make the player respawn) and gives a strong surprise factor in certain scenarios. 

The boss battles are cool due to the gameplay (more on that in a little bit) that may make boss battles repeatitve, but a fun experience.

The cutscenes in Space Marine are above-average to good. Some cutscenes intrigue me (especially the earlier campaign cutscenes due to seeing the environment in Space Marine), other cutscenes bore me as in my opinion, I got the same thought of "same old, same old". In saying that, some cutscenes are repeatitive and predictable. Another criticism of cutscenes is that it is disjointed. For example, before a cutscene, I am holding a Power Axe, the cutscene happens, I am holding a Chainsword. To add to this, the cutscene in a few particular scenes did not correlate with the gameplay at all. For example, in one cutscene I was beaten up (minor spoiler) and the cutscene finishes and it is like nothing happened, it was ridiculous and happened very occasionally in the campaign.

Gameplay: The gameplay in Space Marine is very good. Using Melee is basically hack and slash, which is very fun. The gun gameplay is pretty cool with the sounds, look and gunfights in the game, which I enjoy. Again, the main criticism of this section is that whilst hack and slash is fun, it gets dull further into the game. The involvement of jet packs added another layer to gameplay in this game, and created refreshment in the campaign.

In the final mission of the campaign, the gameplay involved was different than seen throughout the campaign, and I say it was actually very strong. Without spoilers, it involves flying and punching and I found this to be awesome, considering I don't play many games that have that sort of gameplay involved.

Negative Comments: Space Marine contains quite a few bugs, some very visible, some not visible at all to some, but visible to I. The other negative comments have been explained above with the gameplay, cutscenes, and campaign.  Whilst the pros outweigh the cons in Space Marine, the cons impact the game more than expected.

Overall: It is a very solid game, filled with bugs galore, but a fun experience. For I that was introduced to Warhammer 40,000 through Space Marine, I enjoyed a refresh from the typical FPS campaigns, but it is a genre I am not still not eager to play. 

My friend purchased a Humble Bundle which included Warhammer series, and for Steam's price of $39.99, I personally would not recommend it. If I had to purchase this game again after playing it, I would not purchase it for higher than $29.99. I feel this is a fair price point because I have not checked out MP, and considering this game is four years old, no one most likely plays MP. I don't know about the modes so I cannot comment extensively, however older games I tend to purchase knowing I can only play the campaign, and don't have an overly interest in MP. If you play through the campaign on all difficulties, the player can probably get about 30+ hours out of this game. 7/10.



UPDATE #1: I have just found out that there is two co-op modes in Multiplayer (one was patched in, other has to be purchased for $12.99) meaning with four people, you can probably get an extra few hours out of the game.

Also to mention, all DLC is multiplayer-based according to a forum post.
